subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Doping: Adding Impurities on Purpose
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Doping: Adding Impurities on Purpose.

hook.text: Pure silicon is a poor conductor. Add a trace of phosphorus and conductivity soars.

buildup.text: Phosphorus has five outer electrons. Silicon has four. One extra electron is free to roam.

discovery.text: This is N-type doping — extra electrons carry current. P-type uses boron to create holes.

twist.text: Just one dopant atom per million silicon atoms changes conductivity by a factor of 1,000.

climax.text: Every chip in every phone relies on precisely controlled doping to function.

punchline.text: A pinch of impurity turns useless silicon into the heart of all electronics.

quiz.question: What does N-type doping add to silicon?
options: Extra holes that carry positive charge
Extra electrons that act as free charge carriers
Metal atoms that create a conductive layer
